cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: New players experience a punishing introduction where they are matched against veteran players with superior gear, while the core loop starts to feel repetitive due to shallow progression and copy-paste quests.

claims.claim: New players are matched against veteran players with significantly better gear, levels, and experience, creating an unbalanced and punishing player-versus-player experience.

citations.review_text:
Based on my experience, Arc Raiders has some fundamental design issues that make it difficult to recommend.

From the very first open-world missions, new players are routinely matched against veterans with hundreds of hours of experience. The result is that you're often eliminated before you have a meaningful chance to learn the game or build your inventory. Even when you avoid other players, the AI can feel overly punishing, with enemy detection and accuracy sometimes giving the impression that they can track you through cover.

The biggest problem is the lack of progression-based matchmaking or gear balancing. Mixing brand-new players with fully geared, highly experienced players creates a frustrating PvPvE experience where skill progression is overshadowed by massive equipment and experience gaps. A gear score system, beginner protection, or some form of matchmaking based on progression would go a long way toward making the game more approachable.

As it stands today, I'd only recommend Arc Raiders if you already enjoy extremely unforgiving extraction shooters and don't mind spending a significant amount of time being outmatched while learning. For everyone else, there are currently better looter shooters that offer a fairer onboarding experience.

TL;DR - Game is made for people with excessive amounts of time that like to grind.  Terrible for new players. If you don't mind having great gear lost by uninitiated PVP by people that are much higher level than you with max gear, this game is for you.  Otherwise, steer clear unless 90% off.  Play Helldivers 2 if PVP is not your thing.  If PVP is your thing but you don't have a lot of time, I'd also avoid this. The recent review score closer to 50% is more accurate.

Details:
I tried this game out with a few buddies after one of them expressed interest and had already purchased it.  My first game,  two guys with matching skins killed me on sight.   Maybe they were noobs that purchased the skins, and I was just caught unaware as a noob, but I'm doubting that.  I played many more without getting killed, but here are what I think are inherent flaws:

1. There is an experience system with small but real buffs for your character via skill points.  You will be matched with people that are much higher level than you and therefore have an inherently stronger character.  So it's not just "git gud", it's get so good you can overcome inherently stronger players that may have been playing since the game released, or the season started, and have a lot more time than you.

2.  You drop nearly everything you have when killed, including your guns, shield, etc.  If you've spent time or precious resources for higher level stuff, that will all be gone if you die.  Hence my reference to grinding. I haven't even played enough to reach this point, but I can already see the grind necessary just to level up facilities and earn currency.

3.  In line with the previous points, those people with ♥♥♥♥ tons of time or those who cheat will have great gear.  Again, an inherent power difference.  It's not just aim better, use cover, use items, etc better... it's like being level 1 in Wow and being asked to kill the level 40 ganker back in Vanilla.  Only a miracle will save you (like anoth…

claims.claim: The game loop becomes repetitive after a number of hours, with complaints of shallow progression and boring, copy-paste quests.

citations.review_text: THIS IS GENUINELY THE WORST GAME I HAVE EVER PLAYED, Missions feel like copy-paste chores (go to a location, grab an item, extract) with minimal rewards. Once workbenches are maxed out, there is no meaningful progression or objective left to chase. A persistent bug frequently drops squad fills. The community or the team you fill in are mostly toxic players .This is the first ever game i'm even commenting about. THE PAYMENT IS ALL BUT JUST PURE WASTE. Even though i have a maxed out gpu and cpu the game feels terribly laggy.

Not Recommended

I was genuinely excited to buy ARC Raiders because it looked like a fun extraction shooter with interesting PvPvE gameplay. From the trailers and gameplay videos, I expected intense fights, rewarding progression, and an experience that would keep me coming back. Unfortunately, after playing it myself, I was left feeling disappointed.

The biggest issue for me is that the game just isn't fun enough to justify the price. The gameplay becomes repetitive much faster than I expected. Most matches follow the same pattern, and instead of feeling rewarded for taking risks, it often feels like I'm just wasting my time. Losing all of your gear after one bad encounter is part of the extraction genre, but here it often feels frustrating instead of exciting.

The matchmaking also didn't feel balanced. I frequently ended up fighting players who had much better gear and far more experience, making many encounters feel unfair before they even started. Instead of encouraging me to keep improving, it made me feel like I had little chance of competing.

Progression also feels slower than I expected. I spent hours playing but didn't feel like I was making meaningful progress. Unlocks and rewards weren't satisfying enough to make the grind enjoyable, and after a while every session started to feel the same.

I also ran into performance issues and occasional bugs that hurt the experience. Whether it was stuttering, frame drops, or other technical problems, they made the game even less enjoyable than it already was. For a game at this price, I expected a much smoother experience.

Overall, I gave the game a fair chance because I really wanted to enjoy it, but it simply wasn't what I expected. Instead of looking forward to playing, I found myself forcing myself to launch it, hoping it would finally click. It never did.

Because of all of these issues, I honestly regret buying the game and would like a refund. I don't feel that I got my money's worth, and I can't recommend …

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game becomes repetitive and lacks endgame content after reaching higher progression tiers.

citations.review_text: No end game content, cheaters run rampant, very repetitive.

Fun for the First 50 Hours, But Lacks the Depth to Keep You Coming Back

This game was really fun for the first 50 hours, but as someone who isn't a casual gamer, 50 hours is just scratching the surface. Hunting down blueprints is a great hook early on, but once you finish your upgrades, the game falls off a cliff. I can't stress enough how fast this gets boring once you hit the endgame.

The Good
Great Visuals & Performance: The game looks fantastic and runs really well.

Accessible Loop: It is a solid, stress-free entry point for casual players or anyone looking for an easier extraction shooter experience. That is not necessarily a bad thing—it's just not for me.

Why It Falls Short (The Bad)
Shallow PvP & Gunplay: For an extraction shooter, the PvP combat and gun mechanics lack real depth. There just isn't enough mechanical nuance to make firefights rewarding over the long haul.

Annoying PvE: The PvE enemies go from engaging to just plain annoying once you no longer need their parts for upgrades.

Looting Loses Its Value: Looting is only fun when you actually need those items for progress. Once your upgrades and blueprints are done, searching for loot loses all meaning.

No Long-Term Hook: Unlike Delta Force, which keeps me coming back because of its deep PvP, exciting high-tier loot drops (like big reds), and an economy like the auction house, ARC Raiders just doesn't have a lasting endgame loop.

The Verdict
If you want an easy, casual-friendly extraction shooter that looks great and runs smooth, you will probably enjoy your time here. But if you are a hardcore player looking for deep PvP combat and an economy you can grind for hundreds of hours, this gets boring very fast.

Rating: 6/10 (Good for Casuals, Lacks Endgame Depth)

claims.claim: Reviewers state that inventory space is limited while the game requires gathering items for crafting and upgrades.

citations.review_text:
I recently bought this game after watching a bunch of videos and finally biting the bullet to give it a go since it looked amazing, was reviewed amazingly and what not.

But honestly?  I think this game has some of the worst cheating in a shooter... and it feels awful to play when you are constantly running into people cheating.  

My last game that I played, I had a guy on my team called "ICheatMommy" telling us that he was cheating and that he could see every player on the map, running around murdering everyone and then yelling at the enemies telling them to "Shut up ♥♥♥♥♥, I am cheating" on a brand new steam account.  Like how does that get past even a single game???  

I have had items refunded to me through the systems ban system, from encountering cheaters multiple times... While I appreciate the sentiment, my experience was already ruined.  

I also joined right when a dupe exploit was found and every single person I have run into has an obscene amount of bombs and what not...  and players are just like "Oh yeah don't worry about it, they just used the dupe exploit last week" 

I do have other things about the game that I truly dont like - like how many items their are to gather and how limited the inventory space is.  How the balance of the higher tier guns are out of whack, once you have them it feels broken.  The toxicity of some players (pretty normal in shooters).  But none of these are truly game breaking in my opinion, they are just minor negatives in my opinion.

It truly does suck because the games gunplay is phenomenal, the graphics are quite amazing for a shooter and the map design is unparalleled.   Performance is also quite amazing, but that really is quite normal with shooters. 

When I was having fun, I was having a LOT of fun.  But more often then not the game left me frustrated and annoyed because of cheaters and the negatives I listed above.

The game's engine and technical build quality are great, but it fails in its design elements. The graphics are great and the sound is some of the best implemented in gaming. 
It seems like the designers never figured out what they wanted it to be, and so it feels like it fails in many different areas. The biggest problem is that it has an identify crisis as PVE or PVP. There's no dedicated PVP or PVE servers. PVP proponents gripe and complain because PVE-focused players stopped bringing any decent loot with them, so PVPers waste time waiting in ambush, eventually killing players who drop nothing but crummy freeloadouts (a feature that's being surveyed to be eliminated at this time). PVE players have a hard justification to bring anything because battles are usually won by whoever takes the first shot (or grenade toss, or trap kill, etc.). 
A secondary failure is due to spending most of your time in missions scavengering and the game encourages this with missions and rewards for "collecting x numbers of this material to craft or upgrade so-and-so", but your inventory maxes out pretty quickly so you spend a ton of time trying to figure out what you might not need to keep. Unless you have players you already know to jump into a game with, you'll spend almost all your time steering clear of other players because you never know when they might take advantage of battle to shoot you in the back. Because decent weapons require so much time to grab materials to craft, you're taking a big risk anytime you go out with them because you might get them stolen. Without good weapons, enemy bots get too challenging pretty quickly. The result is there really isn't any enjoyment in playing it unless you've got a couple friends outside the game you can count on to watch your back.

claims.claim: Reviewers praise the game's audio design and sound quality.

citations.review_text: The sound design of this game is crazy good.

One of the best PvPvE I've played. Outstanding sound design and acoustics, so crisp, detailed and well localized. Optimized so well it both runs on my home PC (RTX5080S) and Intel Arc laptop. Stylistically beautiful and unique. Good community overall despite some rats and cheaters here and there (hey, rats are people too!)

Devs, please add loadout presets (3-5 pre-packed loadouts for different play styles) so we don't have to dig in our inventory for so long every time before raid. Add a auto-buy or auto-craft items that player defined to be in one of the presets, if they are missing from inventory.

All in all, 10/10, I keep going back everyday.

Amazingly well executed game. I never understood the appeal of these kinds of extraction games, you start a round to collect loot so you are stronger for the next round in which you will collect more loot. But what really shines for me here are the gameplay and the immersion. This is easily one of the most immersive games I've played, in large parts because of the amazing work by the sound team. The gunplay also feels really good, much better than you'd think when watching videos of the game, partly because the physics of the enemies are super fun to experience.
The game kinda feels like a zombie survival game but with robots instead of zombies. You start in your base, get a mission to collect something specific for the settlement or check something out, go out to fulfill that mission, encounter all sorts of different interactions during the mission, and finally go back to the base to share what you have found and stock up for the next assignment.
There are many different progression paths you can follow which really keep the game interesting and always give you something to do.

For me they perfected this genre of game and they are far from done with it, as they have major updates announced as of the time I'm writing this. Big recommendation.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game is overrun with cheaters, hackers, and item dupers, while the anti-cheat system and developer responses are ineffective.

citations.review_text: to many cheaters, devs doing nothing for community and all kinds of dupers

Embark totally has failed this game. every round you get into is filled with cheaters. has one of the worst anti cheats and they do not care about this game AT ALL. this whole game was a money grab. do not buy nor play this game its a waste of money.

For a while, one of the better games to play. Eventually cheaters got the best of this game and is not fun to play anymore unless you even the odds and get cheats yourself. Save your time and money by not investing in this game. You're welcome

There are few examples of a company having what could have been a timeless classic and then leaving it to turn to mould in the cupboard, this is one of them.

Embark would struggle to do a worse job with Arc Raiders if they purposefully tried - cheating and exploiting are extremely prevalent, with what little action they take against it being far too little, far too late.

Pre-teaming runs absolutely rampant, with people using the same visual skins, out of game comms and timing their queue initiation to be in the same lobby, often with teams of anywhere from 3-9, the trials aspect of the game is completely deformed, as the vast majority of people "achieving" cantina being people who cheat, stack entire lobbies through discord and cycle which team does the trial unchallenged, no separation of solo/duo/trio scoreboards - it isn't a challenge in your skill at the game or dedication, it is a challenge in how hard you can exploit and break the matchmaking system.

Cheating rampages alongside the pre-teaming issue, including duplicating items which they have done an unacceptably poor job at resolving multiple times now, every time it returning worse than before, people duplicate entire inventories full of the best PvP firearms and proceed to then pre-team and kill entire lobbies ad nauseum.

There are twitch streamers utilising the same cheats for over a month, streaming every day using said cheats openly with literal guides on how to do what they are and not a single ban in that time, despite the supposed "new and improved" denuvo anticheat.

A single employee being emotionally invested in the success of Arc at Embark would be able to ban these people and get something done. No one cares.

The matchmaking is so scuffed I struggle to find a way to list just how many issues there is - people from out of region stacking in low population server regions such as Oceanic and Asia to pre-team and kill the entire lobby, if you fire back at someone shooting at you it adds to your…

claims.claim: Reviewers note that updates arrive on a very slow, bi-annual schedule, leading to a massive loss in the player base.

citations.review_text: love this game but embark devs really need to pick up the urgency of updates more than 2x a year going from game of the possible decade to losing 50% or more player base is insane to me

I love this game, but right now the cheaters are awful and the content is coming out at a snails pace. Wait until they fix the cheaters and realize that a bi-annual update schedule is ridiculous. I honestly can't understand why they would want to kill their own game so badly.

Well it’s about time. Been avoiding a review for so long since this game has kept me split on an opinion for a while.

As my first extraction shooter I’ve put more than 5 hours into, it was a great experience at the start. For the first 1-2 months of playing, the experience was unmatched. Easily the best experience I’ve had in a video game to date.
The game is solid, but the devs just couldn’t keep up with the playerbase. Stuff that should have been nerfed the next day took weeks (looking at you t-nades) and duped items circulated freely for a long time as well. Updates have been lackluster but satisfactory. Cheaters still plague the game and the anti-cheat has done nothing about it, which is mainly why I don’t do PvP, as whenever I do I always seem to get blatant cheaters in my lobbies. One time I spawned in with a free kit and hid in the top room at TSA and eventually surrendered as I had to go. Didn’t engage in any fights and didn’t use any items in the kit. Next day I got the kit back cause somebody around me was cheating. The devs seem to be saying that it’s in the works, but at the same time we were told that major updates are only every 6 months, which everybody and their mother was upset about.

I’m still recommending this game purely to the past times I had; the first time playing was magical. It’s still a solid game and I will continue to play, just letting you know that the devs are struggling to keep the playerbase engaged with content and don’t care about veteran players and their desires.

10/10 for the first experience
4/10 for the dev team’s engagement with the community
7/10 overall in its current state

claims.claim: Reviewers highlight that weapons degrade too quickly, requiring excessive time spent gathering materials for repairs.

citations.review_text:
Game was great when it came out, but over time they’ve slowly ruined it. 
Guns break wayyyy too fast now, I have to focus almost entirely on gathering materials to repair my weapon from the current raid, and can barely focus on anything else. Especially with the added arc… I love them, but guns need to last longer. The server stability is also still an issue. And I tried to do trials with my Xbox friends last night but was unable to play with him due to them getting an update early… I voiced my discontent about this in their discord and they permanently banned me for it. 

Also the cosmetics are way too damn expensive, $20 for a skin is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ridiculous!

This game 100% rewards bad players and ♥♥♥♥♥ on real players. You can load into a match and do absolutely everything that is asked of you. Then, on your way out, there is just a random guy who trapped the extraction hatch and kills you. None of your hard work even counts.The combat balancing is complete trash. At this point, light shields do not even make sense to use because everything breaks them instantly. Some guns use the same ammo type but hit with wildly different damage, and every single reload takes way too long.The skill tree is garbage because it only gives you minimal stat boosts. It honestly feels like a base player is exactly the same as a player with a fully unlocked skill tree.Then there is the game itself. The story is good only if you do not think about it too deeply. Everything is trying to kill you while you play, and all the enemies feel like they are in god mode. You get two-shot by everything, yet there are free kits available. There is next to no real reason to run a full, expensive kit when you can get everything you need for free. It is zero risk and all reward. On top of that, when you do Trials, they dynamically change the game to make it vastly harder to even complete. The loot for big ARC is thin and mostly less valuable than the actual cost to fight them. Crafting costs a ton, and the bot provided for trading always asks for an excessive amount of resources for random, mid-tier items. Why not just provide a player-to-player market lobby? Another thing that people keep talking about is the customization. Everything is locked into set cosmetic packs. There is no mixing and matching allowed. Because of this, everyone looks exactly the same, just slightly different. This system would make way more sense if the outfits were tied to specific groups or factions in the game, but they are not.

This game goes up there as one of the greatest "what ifs" in gaming. What if the Devs listened to the community? What if they added a PvE or PvP option? Sometimes after work I don't want to be sweaty and PvP. I want to get loot or do missions cause I don't have hours to play during the week. But no, now I have to spend hours getting friendlies just to get some more loot for a few days, PvP on weekends, then have to do it all over again! What if the Devs didn't take our money and run... twice a year major updates?! For a game that had 100k+ daily players on Steam alone? Next update is when GTA 6 comes out? Game is dead and it's a damn shame.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game features excellent graphics, art direction, and visual presentation.

citations.review_text:
I am so impressed by this title, and I have never played anything quite like it. The closest comparison would be Hunt Showdown: also an extraction shooter with permadeath, also with varied and unpredictable AI enemies, also with a unique setting and aesthetic, also with extremely impressive and informative sound design. In a way I am not surprised, as it comes from the devs who gave me such a good time in The Finals. 

Instead of gushing about every minute detail, I will impress upon you the important parts that Arc gets right. The maps are gorgeous and varied, with elevations and changing environments across huge spaces that lead to interesting fights and hairy situations. I love the extraction zones, which are different from map to map but all force you into contact with other potentially dangerous raiders. Gunplay is (again) varied and satisfying, with an attachment and upgrade system (which cleverly does not improve the damage of weapons - a raider who has thrown a pile of resources into ornamenting their favourite gun will not simply overwhelm everyone else), and an array of consumables of all flavours - in 125hrs I have not used (or even seen) all the guns and deployables on offer. The setting is retro-futuristic (think Alien?) and the enemies match this - you are facing a really (again again) unique selection of extremely adaptive and annoying robots. By land and by air, each has their own behaviours and poses a different threat, and the armour system makes fighting each one a small puzzle and poses dilemmas in your loadout selection. The larger foes are suitably terrifying. 

What keeps me here is the depth and variety. Not just in the things already mentioned, but in the progression systems too. There are many, which I think award you progression in gameplay, crafting and customization at a satisfying rate. This includes over 100 quests given to you by NPC's, which flesh out the world and ask you to change your plan and your playstyle to complete them. …

I've played ARC Raiders since launch, and while I had a lot of fun at first, the game quickly became repetitive.

Gameplay – 7/10

The core gameplay is solid. The gunplay feels good, exploring the world is fun, and the PvPvE concept is interesting. The atmosphere and art style are also great.

However, after a while, every raid starts to feel the same. Once you've experienced the core loop, there's not much variety to keep you coming back.

Multiplayer – 7/10

Playing with friends is definitely the best way to enjoy ARC Raiders. The tense extraction moments can be exciting, but after enough hours, the lack of content becomes noticeable.

Unfortunately, I had a feeling this would happen, and I wasn't surprised to see the player base drop so quickly.

Graphics – 9/10

The game looks fantastic. The environments, lighting, and overall art direction are beautiful and help create a unique atmosphere.

Overall Rating

Gameplay: 7/10
Multiplayer: 7/10
Graphics: 9/10

Final Score: 7/10

ARC Raiders is a fun extraction shooter with a strong foundation, but it becomes repetitive too quickly. I enjoyed my time with it, but it didn't keep me playing for long. Hopefully future updates bring more variety and content, because the potential is definitely there.

Arc Raiders is a gorgeous game with great style and huge potential, but right now it’s practically unplayable unless you enjoy rat‑style PvP, cheating, or camping. Embark refuses to add a PvE flag, so every round is filled with players who do nothing but ambush and grief you. If you want to enjoy quests or PvE progression, forget it — you get killed instantly by rats the moment you spawn, and you can’t even shoot back without being thrown into sweatlord PvP lobbies.
Embark clearly doesn’t care, and because of that, the game is already dying. Without PvE players, Arc Raiders has no future — and unless they fix this, it deserves to die early.
---italiano (la mia lingua) ---
Arc Raiders è un gioco bellissimo, con uno stile incredibile e un potenziale enorme, ma al momento è praticamente ingiocabile a meno che tu non ti diverta con il PvP da ratto, cheat o camping. Embark si rifiuta di aggiungere un flag PvE, quindi ogni round è pieno di giocatori che fanno solo imboscate e griefing. Se vuoi goderti le quest o la progressione PvE, scordatelo — vieni ucciso all’istante da ratti appena spawni, e non puoi nemmeno rispondere al fuoco senza finire nelle lobby PvP estreme.
Embark chiaramente se ne frega, e per questo il gioco sta già morendo. Senza i giocatori PvE, Arc Raiders non ha futuro — e se non sistemano questa cosa, merita di morire presto.

The game becomes very boring, very quickly. They delayed the game and spent 2 years adding PvP. They should have spent that on content and the story. There is just nothing to do in the game. Go up, loot, come back. No vision, no story, no point in playing.

Embark has great devs. Great visuals, great music and audio engineering. But the game is just about nothing. Very boring.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as plagued by cheaters, hackers, and item dupers.

citations.review_text: to many cheaters, devs doing nothing for community and all kinds of dupers

Genuinely the most fun PvP I have had in a TPS in recent memory. Some servers are absolutely infested with cheaters which is affirmed as I regularly get notifications that my reports resulted in bans/action taken against their accounts.

Outside of the cheating though, there is nothing on the market currently that comes close to Arc in terms of the highs and lows you get from a PvP environment that is peppered with oppressive PvE enemies.

What started out as something revolutionary became one of the biggest disappointments of 2026. These guys made one of the ultimate blueprints to a game and found every single way to fail it and its community. Embark made their bag and ran away with it. I truly am disappointed by the absolute lack of effort this game has become. Community is nothing but hackers/cheaters now and the game has no heart in it.

There are few examples of a company having what could have been a timeless classic and then leaving it to turn to mould in the cupboard, this is one of them.

Embark would struggle to do a worse job with Arc Raiders if they purposefully tried - cheating and exploiting are extremely prevalent, with what little action they take against it being far too little, far too late.

Pre-teaming runs absolutely rampant, with people using the same visual skins, out of game comms and timing their queue initiation to be in the same lobby, often with teams of anywhere from 3-9, the trials aspect of the game is completely deformed, as the vast majority of people "achieving" cantina being people who cheat, stack entire lobbies through discord and cycle which team does the trial unchallenged, no separation of solo/duo/trio scoreboards - it isn't a challenge in your skill at the game or dedication, it is a challenge in how hard you can exploit and break the matchmaking system.

Cheating rampages alongside the pre-teaming issue, including duplicating items which they have done an unacceptably poor job at resolving multiple times now, every time it returning worse than before, people duplicate entire inventories full of the best PvP firearms and proceed to then pre-team and kill entire lobbies ad nauseum.

There are twitch streamers utilising the same cheats for over a month, streaming every day using said cheats openly with literal guides on how to do what they are and not a single ban in that time, despite the supposed "new and improved" denuvo anticheat.

A single employee being emotionally invested in the success of Arc at Embark would be able to ban these people and get something done. No one cares.

The matchmaking is so scuffed I struggle to find a way to list just how many issues there is - people from out of region stacking in low population server regions such as Oceanic and Asia to pre-team and kill the entire lobby, if you fire back at someone shooting at you it adds to your…

claims.claim: Reviewers report that players camp extraction points and high-value loot rooms to ambush others.

citations.review_text: The game is straight ass. They just keep ruining the game with their updates and the stupid stuff they add. Dying game. Only 20,000-30,000 people on the game nowadays. Sick of making a loadout for a night raid because I can't go into a night raid with a free loadout anymore and having other losers just camping high value loot rooms and extraction points because they know they can get a loadout off you.

100 hours in and this is what i have learned.
1. the worst of mankind will camp like rats. they hide at extracts, small looting rooms, and even hack/cheat with aimbots and similar things. 
2. Devs do not give a rats A$$ about any of it. they just say its supposed to be people against the arc not each other, but keep the game pvpve. 
3. if you do find something really good, refer back to #1. 

not worth ur dime unless u like to lose everything you work for over and over and over again. the arc in the game is hard enough without dbag rats shooting u while ur killing arc. i will not touch this game till they make it pve, not worth the time or effort when the devs do not care whatso ever to manage the behavior of the waste of air in society from ruining every single match u go in. save ur money.

When *ARC Raiders* first launched, it had one of the best communities I've experienced in a long time. People actually talked over voice chat, teamed up, negotiated, and created memorable encounters. The social aspect was what made the game stand out.

Unfortunately, that community has deteriorated over time. Public voice chat has become a mess, with far too many people treating it like a 2010-era Call of Duty lobby, throwing around racial slurs and other toxic garbage. Instead of adding to the experience, voice chat often makes it worse.

Then there are the rats. Players who sit at extraction waiting to ambush people who've spent an entire raid looting, or the ones who refuse to say a single word over voice chat until after they've already downed you. It completely undermines the unique player interactions that originally made the game special. At this point, it feels less like a game of strategy and more like a contest to see who can exploit other players' time the most.

And before anyone says "get good," some of us have careers, families, and responsibilities outside of gaming. I don't have unlimited hours every day to grind or recover from losing everything to someone camping an extract for 20 minutes. I want to play a game where I can make meaningful progress without feeling like every session is wasted.

If the developers aren't willing to separate the PvP experience, then at least let the community host private servers. Give players the ability to create their own rulesets and communities so those of us who enjoyed the original cooperative, social atmosphere have somewhere to play. Right now, the game's biggest problem isn't its mechanics... it's the culture that's developed around them.  

With that said, I've uninstalled at this point... I'm moving on...

This game was amazing when it first came out, the PvP and PvE aspect was amazing. There was something always to do whether it was looting, fighting arc, fighting other players etc.

Now in current day this game is pure hot garbage, want to resource hunt? forget it. Rats, extract campers, unfair exploits. Want to have fun PvP? Even worse experience. I am convinced 30%-40% of the player base is cheating on pc. The worst part is now when you call out a blatant cheater embark does not reimburse your items back despite reporting an obvious cheater. On top of that players are finding exploits now to matchmake in big parties up to 6-9 players all playing on one server killing everyone. This game had a lot of potenial to be a GREAT game, but unfortunately embark has given a middle finger to those who play the game fair and square. Pretty much promoting the game for those who like to cheat and abuse gamebreaking exploits. 

I would not reccomend arc in today's current state. 

Best way to put it. This game is pure ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.
